methodologySummary: RateReveal reference ranges are conservative review signals, not market percentiles or promised processor pricing. The initial entries reuse category-specific ranges only where the repository documents a category-specific MCC basis, current network-cost inputs, broad independent all-in cross-checks, and anonymized Fiserv statement sanity checks. Qualification is restricted to the calibration volume tier, standard-risk card-present merchants, supported Fiserv-family statements, and the registry review period.

sourceRecords.title: Published U.S. Visa and Mastercard interchange schedules, 2025–2026 review set
sourceRecords.supportedClaim: Category and card-program interchange costs are material inputs to an all-in effective-rate reference.
limitations: Interchange schedules do not establish processor markup or a guaranteed all-in merchant price.
Actual card mix and qualification outcomes vary by merchant.

sourceRecords.title: Independent U.S. processing-cost analyses used for broad all-in triangulation
sourceRecords.supportedClaim: The admitted ranges fall inside the broad U.S. all-in cost context documented by multiple independent industry analyses.
limitations: The referenced analyses are directional and do not provide a statistical distribution for every MCC.
The ranges must not be described as an industry standard or guaranteed target.

sourceRecords.title: Anonymized supported-Fiserv statement sanity-check cohort
sourceRecords.supportedClaim: The initial restaurant and grocery ranges were checked against supported Fiserv statement behavior for directional plausibility.
limitations: The cohort is small and is not a representative market sample.
No private merchant identity is part of the merchant-facing source description.

entries.methodology: Category-specific restaurant interchange and network-cost context was combined with broad independent U.S. all-in processing ranges and an anonymized supported-Fiserv sanity check. The base range is admitted only for standard-risk card-present merchants in the $100,000–$500,000 annualized calibration tier.
limitations: This is a RateReveal pricing-review reference, not a market percentile, contract term, or guaranteed target.
Commercial-card mix, debit regulation, ticket size, rewards mix, and transaction qualification can move actual costs.
Card-not-present, mixed-channel, high-risk, and other annual-volume tiers are not covered by this entry.

entries.methodology: Category-specific grocery interchange and network-cost context was combined with broad independent U.S. all-in processing ranges and an anonymized supported-Fiserv sanity check. The base range is admitted only for standard-risk card-present merchants in the $100,000–$500,000 annualized calibration tier.
limitations: This is a RateReveal pricing-review reference, not a market percentile, contract term, or guaranteed target.
Regulated-debit share, specialty-food mix, rewards mix, ticket size, and transaction qualification can move actual costs.
Card-not-present, mixed-channel, high-risk, and other annual-volume tiers are not covered by this entry.

unavailableCoverage.scope: general_retail, professional_services, gas_petroleum, lodging, auto_repair, mobile_phone_repair, ecommerce, and high_risk_retail
unavailableCoverage.reason: Existing repository ranges do not yet have sufficiently specific per-entry methodology and validation for merchant-facing admission.
The existing channel adjustments are directional and are not admitted as a qualified effective-rate range.
Existing volume adjustments are directional assumptions and are not admitted for merchant display.
The initial registry does not claim historical applicability outside its reviewed period.
